fields.why: By the brief's letter, rurality is an SPD needing no extra framing, and rural-county clinic results are reported and described ('Responding rural clinics reported recommending vaccination more frequently than did clinics in the affected city'), which meets level 2 without disparity framing (B). A's level 0 is defensible because the split is really outbreak-affected city vs unaffected areas, about dogs' vaccination at clinics, with no social-position meaning; a rule is needed on whether rurality used only as outbreak geography (or for animal data) counts as an SPD.

The survey reports 'clinics in rural counties' separately and the text describes their results, so rurality as a stratifier is present on the brief's terms; A's exclusion rests on treating it as geography by itself, which the same rule gap leaves open.

brief_issues: Unclear whether rurality counts as an SPD when it only labels outbreak-unaffected areas and the data concern animals (dog vaccination at clinics); also whether 'vaccine-preventable (other)' and vaccine_outcome_type apply when only an animal vaccine exists (both readers used them here).
